assumptions: The right-to-repair regime produces enough incremental documented intake to support a private operational layer.
A narrow appliance category can provide sufficient repairer density in Warsaw.
Retailers will consider paying for completed-case routing rather than building or using public infrastructure.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Signed repairer capacity reservations and one paid anchor intake partner, followed by 100 routed cases demonstrating completion rate, dispute rate, contribution margin, and repeat volume.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Documented repair obligations can increase demand for triage and capacity-aware routing beyond simple directory discovery.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Repair intake consumes labor and consumers pay for repairs, but the payer, routing fee, incremental case volume, and willingness to pay are unresolved.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Transaction and platform fees are plausible, yet low consumer frequency, support, CAC, disputes, supply onboarding, and enterprise sales threaten margins and payback.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: One appliance category in Warsaw is a sensible density-focused test, but repair economics vary sharply and the meaningful serviceable segment is uncertain.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: No capacity, retailer intake, or customer relationship is controlled, and public or incumbent routing can commoditize the discovery layer.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A working network could expand across product categories, cities, warranty administration, insurers, parts logistics, and white-label retail intake.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Completion and repairer-reliability data could compound, but only after scale and without protection from supplier multi-homing or retailer integration.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Confirmed capacity, triage, and evidence could beat directories, but the advantage over native retailer, manufacturer, and future public workflows is unproven.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Newly applicable repair rights create a timely operational need, tempered by the expected public platform and immature demand evidence.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: White-label retailers could provide volume, but agreements are unsigned and consumer search acquisition may be expensive relative to transaction revenue.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The marketplace requires two-sided onboarding, quality control, disputes, dispatch, and support that strain the founder's part-time and low-social-energy constraints.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure an exclusive or deeply integrated retailer intake contract paired with reserved, SLA-backed repair capacity in one category and geography.
main_structural_strength: The concept can add operational value through verified capacity and triage rather than relying solely on repair-provider discovery.
primary_score_limiter: It controls neither demand nor supply, and its payer and unit economics remain unresolved in an operationally intensive marketplace.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The planned European repair platform may commoditize discovery while incumbents retain warranty intake and repairers retain capacity.
